idiom_name: struct holding the driver handle + methods per service (playwright-go or chromedp)
implementation_notes: Go has no classes, but the idiom is direct: a struct holds the driver handle - for example *playwright.Page from playwright-go - and its methods are the services the surface offers, with locators created in the constructor or inside the method and values returned as strings, bools or other page structs. What replaces the classic class hierarchy is composition: pages embed a shared base struct for the driver and navigation helpers, and page objects compose component structs for repeated fragments. The framework's locators re-resolve on every action, so no reflection-style element caching is needed and stale-handle handling is explicit.
pitfalls: Go structs have no destructors: close the browser context and stop the Playwright driver in the test or via t.Cleanup, or the driver process and its bridge outlive the suite.
Errors are values: every page method returns (T, error) and the test checks it; a method that swallows the driver error turns a failed lookup into a mysterious nil dereference later.
Embedding a shared base struct couples every page to one driver type; when a suite mixes chromedp and playwright-go, keep the handle behind a small interface instead of embedding.
